description: A geometry library for engineering drawings and models, in two dimensions and in three. Points, vectors, lines, polylines, polygons, faces with holes, circles and oriented rectangles in the plane; points, planes, triangles, polygons, faces, solids, boxes, coordinate systems and transformations in space. Over both: distance, projection, containment, intersection, collision, parallelism, parametrization, merging, splitting, extending and trimming, offsetting, and boolean operations. It also reads, writes and edits DXF drawings with AutoCAD's names, carries the label placement that arranges drawing labels clear of each other and of blocked regions, and packs boxes such as drawing views onto sheets of paper. Every comparison is tolerance-aware, because coordinates that come out of a BIM model are never exact.
releaseNotes:
NEW IN 13.10.0

      A minor release: public members added, none removed or renamed. A drawing only read and saved is written as it
      was, to the byte.

      NEW, DXF: shapes typed
      - The entities give their shapes typed, by CadConvert's names: DxfLine.ToGeoLine3() and ToGeoLine2(), and the same
        on DxfCircle, DxfArc, DxfEllipse (ToGeoEllipse of a whole one, ToGeoSpline of a part), DxfRay, DxfXline,
        DxfSpline, DxfDBPoint, DxfLeader, DxfFace, DxfSolid, and the polylines (ToGeoPolyline, ToGeoPolylineArc,
        ToGeoPolygon, ToGeoPolygonArc; the straight two on DxfPolyline3d).
      - In space, the shape GetGeometry() gives, to the bit; in the plane, what DxfReader reads with PlanAs2D, to the
        bit, an entity off the floor refused rather than its z dropped: the line from (0, 0, 0) to (100, 50, 0) is the
        GeoLine2 from (0, 0) to (100, 50), and with a z of 5 at one end ToGeoLine2 refuses it.
      - A polyline is given as the kind asked for: a loop joins the last vertex to the first, a chain of a closed one
        runs back to its first vertex, a straight kind refuses an arc rather than cut it into chords.

      NEW, DXF: the way back
      - SetFromGeCurve takes the shapes of the plane (written at z 0 on the normal up), and the polylines take chains
        and loops: within the point tolerance of the polyline's own plane on its own normal, so a mirrored polyline
        stays mirrored; otherwise in their own plane; a chain on a line off that plane is refused, never flattened.
      - The handle, layer, look and extended data are kept; a shape written as the current one leaves the record as it
        is, widths and fitting and all.

      Details in CHANGELOG.md.

      Earlier releases: https://github.com/nguyenthanguth/GeometryHelper/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
